speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash and tell me exactly when it first appeared? Also, have you noticed any red, swollen, or painful joints lately?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the facial rash have a distinct "slapped cheek" appearance, and has the rash on her body developed a lacy or net-like pattern? I also need to know if she has had any recent contact with other children who had similar symptoms.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The "slapped cheek" appearance and lacy rash pattern strongly suggest Erythema Infectiosum, but I need to confirm a few final details. Does the patient have any history of anemia or immunocompromise, and has she attended school or daycare recently?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Attends local school. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No recent travel history.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the classic "slapped cheek" facial rash and lacy body rash following a viral prodrome in a school-aged child, the diagnosis is clear. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease).
